The monsoon trough remains to our north and west late this afternoon
with drier weather prevailing across the Marianas. Drier conditions 
will persist for another day or two before the monsoon trough sags 
southward. Shower and thunderstorm chances will begin to increase on 
Saturday with scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms possible 
as early as Saturday evening and likely continuing through the 
weekend and into next week. Model guidance differs significantly on 
the potential development of Invest 92W with much uncertainty in the 
forecast around the middle of next week. Regardless, residents of the
Marianas should continue to monitor the forecast over the coming 
days and anticipate increasing wind, shower coverage, and 
thunderstorm chances around the middle of next week.

Marine...
Moderate to fresh winds are expected to persist into the weekend with
the strongest winds being around Tinian and Saipan. Strong gusts will
be possible. Winds will subside to gentle to moderate by late this
weekend. Combined seas of 6 to 9 feet will continue to slowly subside
into weekend and seas have fallen below 10 feet per altimetry data, 
so have cancelled the Small Craft Advisory a little early. The 
westerly, monsoon swell will continue to slowly wane but will likely 
keep hazardous surf and high rip current conditions along west- 
facing reefs going through at least Friday afternoon. Have extended 
the High Surf Advisory and High Risk of Rip Currents products through
5 PM Friday. Another extension into the weekend may be warranted
depending on the monsoon swell.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Depression Nangka (16W) formed late Wednesday night to the
northwest of the northern CNMI, but then exited Guam's Area of 
Responsibility (AOR) this morning as it lifted north of 25N. Nangka 
was later upgraded to a tropical storm this afternoon and is expected
to continue its north-northeast trek over the next few days.

The Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) opened two areas of interest
today, Invest 92W and Invest 93W. Invest 93W is currently located 
around 22N138E, roughly 250 miles southwest of Iwo To and 750 miles 
northwest of Guam, and has quickly become the subject of a Tropical 
Cyclone Formation Alert, meaning that development into a significant 
tropical cyclone (tropical depression) is expected within the next 24
hours. Latest scatterometry data reveals a small, elongated surface 
circulation with 20 to 25 knot winds to the south of 93W's center, 
and 15 to 20 knot winds to the west and north. 93W is expected to
shift east-northeast over the next few days, and looks to pass near
Iwo To to its south late tonight through Friday, slowing down east 
of the island Friday night, then likely exiting the AOR by Saturday 
morning. No direct impacts are expected from Invest 93W, but its
development may help to enhance the monsoon pattern to its south,
helping to increase shower chances for the Marianas this weekend
through early next week.

Invest 92W, formerly Invest 90W, is located to the north of Kosrae 
and Pohnpei near 10N162E. Himawari visible satellite imagery reveals 
an elongated circulation extending from northwest to southeast across
the westernmost atolls of the RMI, with patchy convection seen along
its southern and western flanks this afternoon. 92W is currently 
rated as "sub-low" for development, meaning it is unlikely to develop
into a significant tropical cyclone in the next few days. 92W looks 
to remain relatively stationary over the next 24 hours as it tilts 
slowly westward, merging with the weak area of vorticity to the 
south-southwest of Majuro. 92W then looks to gradually shift west-
northwest as an elongated circulation or an open surface trough, 
promoting heavier showers, thunderstorms, and gusty winds across 
eastern and central Micronesia through the weekend and early next 
week. Around midweek, 92W looks to make a turn to the northwest, 
exiting Micronesia as it moves in the general direction of the CNMI. 
92W is currently very weak and disorganized, and uncertainty remains 
high in its eventual development and track. Nevertheless, the 
disturbance looks to bring a wetter, gustier pattern for Kosrae, 
Pohnpei, and Chuuk over the next few days, and potentially the 
Marianas next week.

For more information on Invest 92W and Invest 93W, please see 
bulletins issued by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) under 
WMO header ABPW10 PGTW and WTPN21 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
The early development stage of Invest 92W will be the primary 
weathermaker for Pohnpei and Kosrae over the next day or two, 
followed by a surge in equatorial moisture pulling northward into 
92W through the weekend. High-end (50% chance) scattered to numerous 
showers and isolated thunderstorms are evident on visible satellite 
imagery and may persist at least through the middle of next week.
